root_cause: claim_due stamped one expires_at for the whole batch of up to 100 jobs and ran them sequentially without renewal; any job finishing after the shared 30 s deadline made _terminal_update raise, aborting the tick. The next claim re-queued the same batch (attempts +1 per claim, no cap, no dead-letter exit), so the same job id stalled the loop. Every claim also selected and json-parsed payload_json of the whole due backlog inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and the controller wrote the alive file in finally so the container stayed healthy.

contract_changes.lease: claim_due only reserves (token + placeholder lease, lease_started=0, attempts NOT incremented). begin_job(job) starts the job's own lease (now + lease_seconds) and is the only place an attempt is counted. run_pending calls it immediately before each job, so claim time and earlier jobs never consume a job's lease.
contract_changes.completion_fencing: The token is the fence, not the clock. A completion/failure/deferral with the CURRENT token is accepted even if the lease clock lapsed, because expiry recovery re-tokens the row. A superseded token still raises (message 'stale distillation lease completion' unchanged; new subclass DistillationLeaseError of DistillationError). The test that pinned raise-and-stay-leased for an expired-but-current lease (test_expired_lease_cannot_commit_any_terminal_outcome_before_reclaim) was replaced deliberately by test_lapsed_lease_is_fenced_by_token_not_by_clock: current token accepted before reclaim, every terminal outcome rejected after reclaim.
contract_changes.per_job_isolation: run_pending catches DistillationLeaseError per job, records the job id in DistillationRunResult.lease_lost and continues. The controller raises stage 'lease_lost' (degraded, names the job ids) after the batch.
contract_changes.expiry_bound: _recover_expired handles at most 200 rows per claim. A lease that expired after the job started increments lease_expiries, re-queues with exponential backoff (30 s * 2^(n-1), cap 1 h; applies to budget-deferred rows too, which keep deferred_since), and at DISTILLATION_JOB_MAX_LEASE_EXPIRIES (default 5) moves to distillation_dead_letters with reason 'lease_expired_repeatedly: n lease expiries'. A lease that expired before the job started is released with no penalty and no attempt. redispatch/redrive reset the counters.
contract_changes.claim_bound: claim_due reads at most `limit` rows per status in index order (distillation_outbox_due_idx, no temp b-tree, asserted by EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in test) plus a window of 500 budget-deferred rows via a partial index, and parses only those payloads. due_tenants is bounded the same way. Demand ranking therefore applies within that window, not across an unbounded backlog (residual: a deferred backlog larger than 500 is ranked by enqueue order beyond the window).
contract_changes.health: The alive marker is no longer refreshed after DISTILLATION_CONTROLLER_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILED_TICKS (default 5) consecutive hard-failed ticks, so the existing alive-file healthcheck turns unhealthy. Stage 'registry_sync' (durable retry/DLQ remains, work is tracked) does not count as hard; any other stage does. One successful tick restores it. docker-compose.yml was not edited.

attempts_normalisation: One-time migration (runs when the lease_expiries column is first added): non-terminal rows with last_error='lease_expired_before_registry_ack' get attempts=0; other non-terminal rows with attempts>=max_attempts are clamped to max_attempts-1; inbox attempts follow. Test: attempts=4321 row is normalised to 0 and then completes (test_inflated_attempts_from_the_expiry_loop_are_normalised_once). Terminal rows are untouched.
schema_compatibility: Additive only: columns lease_expiries, lease_started, pruned_at on distillation_outbox and four partial indexes. The previous accepted release ignores unknown columns and its INSERT/UPDATE statements still work (new columns have defaults). Previous release still reads: all jobs and their payloads except pruned terminal ones; a pruned version holds the marker {"_pruned":true} and only matters if an operator redispatches a terminal job older than the retention (source_for_job returns None, the job fails with 'SourceRecord not found'); recorded as residual. Rolling back leaves lease_expiries/pruned_at unused.

growth_bound.prune: queue.prune() runs each controller tick on at most 500 rows per kind through partial indexes (cost independent of history): terminal (done/skipped/failed) outbox rows older than DISTILLATION_QUEUE_TERMINAL_RETENTION_SECONDS (default 7 d) have their source payload replaced by a marker and their inbox row deleted; resolved dead letters older than DISTILLATION_QUEUE_DEAD_LETTER_RETENTION_SECONDS (default 30 d) are deleted. The outbox row (job_id, idempotency_key, digest, outcome) survives so catch_up never re-enqueues a pruned version (test_prune_bounds_payloads_but_keeps_idempotency).
growth_bound.compaction: Replacing a payload leaves its leaf page allocated and rowid appends do not refill it, so measured file size did not shrink after prune alone (228 MB -> 228 MB). The controller therefore runs queue.compact() (VACUUM + wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE) once 64 MiB of payload bytes have been pruned (process-local counter).

measurement_hosted_shape.dataset: 52,000 jobs, ~2.95 KB payload each (46,000 done + 6,000 pending, SQLite WAL), synthetic but the same schema and size order as the 158 MB hosted queue

growth_bound.growth_per_day_and_cap: Per 1,000 jobs/day: before this change ~3.0 MB/day of payload accumulates forever (plus ~0.7 MB row overhead); after it payload is capped at retention_days * jobs_per_day * ~3 KB (7 d: ~21 MB per 1,000 jobs/day) and only ~0.7 MB/day of row overhead is retained permanently. The hosted jobs/day rate could not be read from this environment; the 158 MB file corresponds to ~52k rows at this shape, so at that volume the cap is ~36 MB after compaction plus 7 d of payload. Retained forever (not pruned, residual): outbox rows. Per-tick queue.metrics() still does an index-only GROUP BY over them (ms at 52k rows).

claim_measurement.dataset: same 52k-row queue with 6,000 due pending jobs
claim_measurement.note: old cost scales with the due backlog (payload select+parse+Python sort), new cost with `limit`

AND available_at<?) with no TEMP B-TREE (asserted in test_claim_reads_a_bounded_number_of_rows_and_never_sorts_on_disk, which also asserts <=7 payload parses for a limit of 7 over 3,000 due rows).

other_per_tick_scans_removed: controller list_all() of every job to build terminal_drafts -> recent_terminal_drafts(limit=200) via the (status, processed_at) partial index
list_dead_letters() with payloads twice per tick -> dead_letter_count() (COUNT only)

acceptance_mapping.10: 144 passed across the five listed files

post_deploy_checks: Container log for pantheon-strategy-distillation-worker-1: first tick after restart no longer prints 'expired distillation lease completion: distill-072acfc4c675f05acdf08a03'.

SELECT status, attempts, lease_expiries FROM distillation_outbox WHERE job_id='distill-072acfc4c675f05acdf08a03' -> attempts reset to 0 by the migration, then status done (or skipped), or after 5 real expiries a dead_letter row with reason lease_expired_repeatedly.
Loop record strategy_distillation turns from failing to success; controller_state consecutive_failures returns to 0.

distill_job_queue.jsonl shrinks (pruning then compaction, ~100 ticks at 500 rows/tick for ~50k terminal rows) and the worker's disk write rate drops from the 53.8 GB/5.8 h seen on 2026-11-17 (the seed-store rewrite part is DISTILLATION-SEED-STORE-BOUNDED-WRITE-20261117).
If ticks keep failing with a non-registry stage, the controller_alive file stops updating after 5 ticks and the container reports unhealthy.
residual_findings: catch_up only considers the first `limit` (100 from the controller) eligible source records each tick (pre-existing slice), so sources beyond that are never admitted by it; not changed here.
Claim tenant filter (EXISTS + json_extract) still scans foreign-tenant rows ahead of the LIMIT when a tenant is passed.
Redispatching a terminal job older than the retention fails with 'SourceRecord not found' because its payload was pruned.

The claim placeholder lease equals lease_seconds; with several concurrent workers a batch longer than that can be reclaimed by a peer, in which case the first worker's begin_job raises DistillationLeaseError and skips the job (safe, but wasteful).
Outbox rows themselves (~0.7 KB each) are retained forever to keep idempotency keys.
